{{Quote|Well let me make it ''simple'' for you. That's a garbage scow. And the salvage yard that uses that kind of Arkon II level transports in this sector is located on—|Tarr Kligson to Jango Fett, advising the latter to look for a garbage scow on Halliron-7|<ref name="JF2" />}}
'''Garbage scows''' were a model of [[starship]]. Around [[33 BBY]], the [[Chevin]] [[Renzoh Silliac]] was hired to [[transport]] the [[thief]] [[Nakano Lash]] in [[Renzoh Silliac's garbage scow|one]] of his garbage scows to his [[Renzoh Silliac's salvage yard|salvage yard]] on the astronomical object [[Hallitron-7]], but ultimately booked her on a [[Commuter ship|commuter shuttle]] headed to [[Roxuli|another destination]] after learning those who had hired him wanted to [[Death|kill]] the thief. Helped by the [[bounty hunter]] [[Tarr Kligson]], the [[bounty]] [[Hunting|hunter]] [[Jango Fett]] tracked down the garbage scow to Hallitron-7.

==Characteristics==
Garbage scows were a [[starship]] model that featured a [[cockpit]], [[Comm unit|communications systems]],<ref name="LOTJ" /> and [[engine]]s.<ref name="JF2" />

==History==
{{Quote|I was paid…a lot…to transport the thief and the statue here for pickup hidden in one of my scows.|Renzoh Silliac to Jango Fett|<ref name="JF2" />}}
At the onset of the [[Great Hyperspace Disaster]]<ref name="LOTJ" /> in [[232 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> [[Hetzal system]] [[scantech]]s [[Merven Getter]] and [[Vel Carann]] issued a [[Star system|system]]-wide alarm warning of the unexpected objects entering their area of [[Realspace|space]], with the former contemplating how their message would be heard everywhere, including the cockpits of garbage scows.<ref name="LOTJ" />

[[File:GarbageScowHologram-JangoFett2.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Tarr Kligson helped Jango Fett track a garbage scow to Hallitron-7.]]
On the astronomical object [[Jaloria]]<ref name="JF2" /> around [[33 BBY]],<ref name="33 BBY">{{JangoFettSeriesDate}}</ref> a replica of the [[Hope of Glee Anselm]] artifact on display during a [[Anselmi–Nautolan treaty|treaty]] ceremony—which its participants believed to be the real artifact—was [[Heist of the Hope of Glee Anselm|stolen]] by [[Unidentified thief group|several]] thieves, including the [[Nautolan]] [[Nakano Lash]].<ref name="JF3">[[Jango Fett 3|''Jango Fett'' 3]]</ref> The [[Chevin]] [[Renzoh Silliac]] was hired to transport Lash and the artifact via [[Renzoh Silliac's garbage scow|one]] of his [[Arkon II level transport]] garbage scows to his [[Renzoh Silliac's salvage yard|salvage yard]] on the astronomical object [[Hallitron-7]]. However, when he learned that those who had hired him intended to [[Death|kill]] Lash instead, he wanted to save her life and booked her on a [[Commuter ship|commuter shuttle]] scheduled to make a supply drop on<ref name="JF2" /> the [[planet]]<ref name="JF3">[[Jango Fett 3|''Jango Fett'' 3]]</ref> [[Roxuli]] before continuing on to<ref name="JF2" /> the planet<ref name="LOTJ" /> [[Coruscant]].<ref name="JF2" />

Not long after, an [[Unidentified human information broker|information broker]] on Coruscant became aware of a lone garbage scow that had left Jaloria after it had been locked down via a recording reflected off a [[Unidentified comm satellite|comm satellite]]. When the [[bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett]] embarked on a search for the thieves who had taken the artifact, the [[Information broker|informant]] presented him with a [[datapad]] showing the recording of the garbage scow. [[Tarr Kligson]], a friend of Fett, tried to gather information on the garbage scow but found that all records of it had been scrubbed.<ref name="JF2" /> He<ref name="BH36">[[Bounty Hunters 36|''Bounty Hunters'' 36]]</ref> reported this to Fett, and told the [[Hunting|hunter]] that the ship was a garbage scow, similar to the ones found in the junkyards of Hallitron-7. There, Fett [[Mission to Hallitron-7|interrogated]] Silliac, who admitted to his part in being hired to transport Lash and the artifact with his garbage scow.<ref name="JF2" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:JangoFett-2-Final-Cover.jpg|thumb|right|175px|In the current canon, garbage scows made their first full appearance in ''Jango Fett'' 2.]]
In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], garbage scows were mentioned in [[The High Republic: Light of the Jedi|''Light of the Jedi'']], a [[2021]] novel written by [[Charles Soule]]<ref name="LOTJ" /> as part of the ''[[Star Wars: The High Republic]]'' multimedia project's [[Phase I: Light of the Jedi|Phase I]].<ref name="Phase I">{{HighRepublicReaderGuide}}</ref> Prior to its release, a mention of the ship was included in a [[StarWars.com]] preview for the novel on [[November 12]], [[2020]].<ref name="Excerpt">{{SW|url=news/light-of-the-jedi-exclusive-excerpt|text=Explore ''Light of the Jedi'' in ''Star Wars: The High Republic'' - Exclusive Excerpt}}</ref> A garbage scow made its first full appearance in the [[Jango Fett 2|second issue]] of the [[2024]] [[Star Wars: Jango Fett (comic series)|''Star Wars: Jango Fett'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic-book]] miniseries. The issue was written by [[Ethan Sacks]], penciled by [[Luke Ross]],<ref name="JangoFett2">[[Jango Fett 2|''Jango Fett'' 2]]</ref> and published by [[Marvel Comics]] on [[April 24]], 2024.<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/114361/star_wars_jango_fett_2024_2|text=Star Wars: Jango Fett (2024) #2}}</ref>

In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, [[Garbage scow/Legends|garbage scows]] were first introduced in ''[[Lando Calrissian and the Starcave of ThonBoka]]'', a [[1983]] novel written by [[L. Neil Smith]] as the third installment of the ''[[Star Wars: The Lando Calrissian Adventures]]'' trilogy.<ref name="ThonBaka">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Starcave of ThonBoka]]''</ref> In the real world, [[Wikipedia:Garbage scow|garbage scows]] are large watercraft used to transport waste and garbage across waterways.<ref name="IRLDefinition">{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/07/31/nyregion/disco-rice-other-trash-talk-picking-up-garbage-means-picking-up-lingo.html|text=''Disco Rice, and Other Trash Talk; Picking Up the Garbage Means Picking Up the Lingo''|author=[[Wikipedia:Ian Urbina|Ian Urbina]]|date=2004-07-31|work=[[Wikipedia:The New York Times|''The New York Times'']]|archivedate=20240117032918}}</ref>
